READABILITY.evidence: Names are clear (`instances_without_deferred`), but no comment explains why parents with deferred fields are skipped. The `if (instance is not None and not ...is_cached(rel_obj))` guard is unexplained, and its formatting is heavier than the surrounding code.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: The same dict comprehension and guard block is copy-pasted into three get_prefetch_queryset methods (ForwardManyToOne, ReverseOneToOne, reverse-FK manager). The reference needed one two-line change. The deferred-field filtering is extra logic beyond the fix.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: No exception problems. But `if not inst.get_deferred_fields()` silently drops reverse-cache population for any parent loaded with only()/defer(), so accessing child.parent can issue extra queries. It also calls get_deferred_fields once per parent instance.

C7-05-CASE1.evidence: The guard does include `not self.field.is_cached(rel_obj)` and covers the one-to-one path. But it also skips any parent with `get_deferred_fields()`, which is a deferred-field hack: a plain `.only(...).prefetch_related('profile_set')` no longer sets child.user, so accessing it costs extra queries.
